meeting_header:
Date: 2027-02-10 | Start: 10:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Sam Rodriguez (Marten Labs VP Eng), Leila Chen (Platform Eng), Omar Farouk (Security), Nina Park (SRE)
summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Reviewed performance benchmarks (latency/throughput), network routing blockers, recent upgrade to runtime v3.4 and kernel changes, and security questions around KMS/HSM and audit logs. Agreed on next steps to run longer sequence benchmarks, finalize VPC peering config, and confirm key management approach.
topics: 1) Bench results and TK of 99p latency 2) VPC peering, route tables, NAT/IGW, Transit Gateway considerations 3) Private deployment upgrade to runtime v3.4 and rollback plan 4) Security/KMS and audit log retention 5) Next steps and timeline
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll try to keep this to 45, quick roll call.
[00:08] Sam: Yep, Sam here. Leila and Omar as well.
[00:12] Priya: Priya from Redwood, I have the perf charts ready.
[00:18] Leila: Good morning.
[00:22] Alex: Cool. Quick agenda: perf review, network blockers, runtime upgrade items, security. Priya, take it away on perf.
[00:30] Priya: Sure. So we re-ran the E2E bench with the small dataset you sent, 1k requests over 30 minutes. Warm cache we saw avg latency around 120ms per token on the rtx-like nodes, 95th at 340ms, 99th at 620ms when KV cache hits. Cold start spikes up to ~2.1s for model load on the initial container.
[00:58] Sam: That 99th seems a bit high compared to what we saw on the hosted API, is that from the network or the model warm-up?
[01:06] Priya: Good question. We instrumented tracing, and most of the tail is on the model decode loop + occasional GC pauses in the container when memory hits thresholds; also some request routing hop because of your NAT gateway setup.
[01:20] Leila: We do have a stateful proxy in front of the subnets for observability reasons, might be adding ~70-100ms.
[01:28] Priya: Yep, that's consistent. If you can remove the proxy for the pilot or put traffic path direct to the inference nodes we drop the 95/99 by ~60-80ms.
[01:38] Nina: Quick, is that safe re: security? The proxy adds WAF and logging we need.
[01:44] Omar: We can limit access with SGs, and rely on host-level logging; WAF is nice but for the pilot scope maybe we can allow direct paths under a locked CIDR.
[01:53] Alex: Note: we'll put the NAT/IGW and egress rules in the diagram we'll send.
[01:59] Priya: Also, we pushed runtime v3.4 to your staging cluster last night; it has a new kernel selection path and quantization fixes. Bench on v3.4 shows 6-8% latency improvement on mixed sequences and better KV cache management.
[02:14] Sam: I saw the upgrade but didn't run long tests yet. Any risks?
[02:18] Priya: The main risk is the new allocator when memory is near saturation; we added a fallback flag to revert to v3.3 behavior. We tested canary with 10% traffic for 2 hours without errors.
[02:29] Leila: We hit one crash during canary yesterday in the secondary node, logs attached to the cloudwatch link you sent but the process restarted automatically. Could be a sidecar probe flapping.
[02:40] Priya: Right, that aligns with an liveness probe timing issue. We'll adjust probe thresholds and push a patch; not a model runtime bug.
[02:49] Alex: On routing, status? Leila, you mentioned there was a blocking route to the Redwood private endpoint.
[02:55] Leila: Yes, the Transit Gateway policy currently denies the peering CIDR, and our infra team needs exact source CIDRs to allow. Also for peered accounts the route table needs the blackhole detection turned off for the route.
[03:08] Alex: We'll provide exact CIDRs and a step-by-step peering checklist. Also include required SG ports: 443 outbound to Redwood private endpoint, 10250 for node health (optional), and ICMP for path MTU.
[03:22] Nina: Path MTU? We saw fragmented packets when large payloads go through the proxy.
[03:27] Priya: Yes, model responses can exceed MTU in some tracing payloads — we recommend enabling tcp-mss clamp or increased MTU on the peering.
[03:36] Omar: What about key management? We need assurance about HSM or KMS integration and whether Redwood stores any plaintext model data.
[03:44] Alex: Redwood Private can integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS or CloudHSM). By default keys never leave your KMS, Redwood uses envelope encryption. We do not persist raw request content outside your cluster unless you opt into analytics.
[03:58] Omar: Can we get the SOC2 audit artifact and key handling diagram?
[04:02] Jordan: Yes, I'll send the security pack and SOC2 section, plus an HSM design note.
[04:08] Leila: Also need audit log retention windows — we want 12 months. Is that configurable?
[04:12] Alex: Yes, retention is configurable; default is 90 days but we can extend to 12 months under the Private contract.
[04:18] Priya: Back to perf: another leaky bucket was batch sizing. When batch size hits >32 on these nodes we see tail latency increase due to memory pressure; optimal batch around 12-16 for your request mix. We're recommending adaptive batching with a 25ms max wait and aggressive cache reuse.
[04:34] Sam: Will adaptive batching hurt latency for small conversational calls?
[04:37] Priya: We tune by route; for low-latency routes you set max batch to 8 and low wait, for high-throughput async jobs you push to 32+.
[04:45] Leila: For the pilot we want two routes: fast-chat and bulk-embed.
[04:49] Alex: Good call. We'll ship a sample config with two routes and suggested autoscale thresholds.
[04:55] Nina: Any update on the model fallback tests — swapping to quantized variant when GPU memory tight?
[05:00] Priya: We ran simple fallback tests; switching to the int8 quantized variant causes a step down in quality but drops memory by ~40% and latency by ~20%. We'll include a degrade policy that falls back only on sustained memory pressure and not on single request spikes.
[05:16] Sam: Can we see transcripts comparing outputs before we enable fallback?
[05:20] Priya: Yes, we'll capture A/B diffs for a sample prompt set and share as a spreadsheet link.
[05:26] Alex: Anything else on upgrades? Rollback plan is a single flag to revert to v3.3 for the runtime, and we keep a 2-hour canary with auto-rollback on error rate >1.5%.
[05:38] Leila: Sounds good. Network ask again: we'll need exact CIDRs, peering steps, and the new recommended MTU/tcp-mss settings.
[05:46] Alex: I'll send that today.
[05:50] Jordan: I'll add the exec check-in for 2/24 and summarize the pilot KPIs we should report: 99p latency, cost/unit, error rate, and cache hit rate.
[06:01] Sam: One last item — pricing for dedicated nodes once we move past pilot, can you share a ballpark?
[06:06] Alex: Yes, we'll include committed capacity pricing and burst/overage model in the follow-up.
[06:12] Nina: Ok. Thanks everyone.
[06:15] Alex: Great, recap: Priya runs long 8k seq bench, Alex sends network diagram, Omar confirms KMS needs, Jordan schedules exec check-in. Meeting adjourned.
[06:28] (end)
